subject.title: [Bug] PTY silently disabled in sandbox mode without warning when pty:true is set

question: For explicit `pty: true` in sandboxed exec, should OpenClaw warn and continue without PTY, or reject the tool call?
rationale: The source repro is clear, but changing how a sandbox capability denial is exposed affects operator-visible security semantics and needs maintainer intent.

options.title: Warn and continue
options.body: Emit a clear warning through the existing exec warnings channel while preserving current sandboxed non-PTY execution behavior.

options.title: Fail explicit PTY
options.body: Reject sandboxed exec calls that explicitly request PTY so users must choose a different execution mode.

options.title: Adopt fork PR after decision
options.body: Use the open fork PR only after maintainers choose semantics and require current proof against main.

recommendation.title: Warn and continue
recommendation.body: Emit a clear warning through the existing exec warnings channel while preserving current sandboxed non-PTY execution behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest history across exec PTY support, fallback behavior, and docs.
